metadata.topic: Reproduction — Sex Hormones of the Menstrual Cycle
metadata.note: 2m: name the TWO sex hormones associated with the menstrual cycle. Oestrogen(1m) + Progesterone(1m). 2 slots × 1m. Context: 28-day menstrual cycle (Anna). Common error: testosterone (male hormone) or FSH/LH (pituitary, not sex hormones per se).

question.name: CSEC Bio May 2022 Q6a(i) — Name the Two Sex Hormones of the Menstrual Cycle
question.text:
Name the TWO sex hormones which are associated with the menstrual cycle:

Hormone 1: [[1]]

Hormone 2: [[2]]
question.general_feedback:
Sex hormones of the menstrual cycle:

  1. Oestrogen (Estrogen) — produced by the ovarian follicle (and corpus luteum); causes thickening of the uterine lining in the first half of the cycle (follicular phase); triggers LH surge at ovulation.
  2. Progesterone — produced mainly by the corpus luteum after ovulation; maintains and further thickens the uterine lining in the second half of the cycle (luteal phase); inhibits menstruation during pregnancy.

Note: FSH and LH are pituitary hormones that control the cycle but are not the sex hormones. Testosterone is the primary male sex hormone (though females produce small amounts).

groups.label: Sex hormone produced during the follicular phase
groups.diagnostic_hint: Oestrogen (also spelled Estrogen) is produced by the developing follicle. It causes the uterine lining to thicken and triggers the LH surge that leads to ovulation.

groups.label: Sex hormone produced by the corpus luteum after ovulation
groups.diagnostic_hint: Progesterone is produced by the corpus luteum after ovulation. It maintains the uterine lining for possible implantation. If no fertilisation occurs, progesterone levels drop and menstruation begins.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 6 tokens for 2 slots. Both slots share the same options. Oestrogen and Progesterone are both correct for either slot — student must select both (one per slot) for full marks. 'Estrogen' is the American spelling of oestrogen — both accepted. 'Testosterone' is the primary male sex hormone; females produce trace amounts but it is not a menstrual cycle hormone. 'FSH' (follicle-stimulating hormone) is a pituitary hormone that controls the cycle but is not itself a sex hormone. 'Adrenaline' is the stress hormone (adrenal medulla) — unrelated.
